arxiv-1802-02181.title: Applications of a Graph Theoretic Based Clustering Framework in Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
arxiv-1802-02181.creator: Yonatan Tariku Tesfaye
arxiv-1802-02181.description: Abstract Abstract R ecently , several clustering algorithms have been used to solve variety of problems from different discipline. This dissertation aims to address different challenging tasks in computer vision and pattern recognition by casting the problems as a clustering problem.

arxiv-1807-05808.title: Pluricomplex Green’s functions and Fano manifolds
arxiv-1807-05808.creator: Nicholas McCleerey, Valentino Tosatti
arxiv-1807-05808.description: Abstract We show that if a Fano manifold does not admit Kähler-Einstein metrics then the Kähler potentials along the continuity method subconverge to a function with analytic singularities along a subvariety which solves the homogeneous complex Monge-Ampère equation on its complement, confirming an expectation of Tian-Yau. Keywords. Fano manifold; pluricomplex Green function; algebraic Kähler potentials 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification.

arxiv-2207-10272.description: Abstract . In this paper, we consider the cutoff Boltzmann equation near Maxwellian, we proved the global existence and uniqueness for the cutoff Boltzmann equation in polynomial weighted space for all γ ∈ ( − 3 , 1 ] \gamma\in(-3,1] .

arxiv-2210-08817.title: PACIFIC: Towards Proactive Conversational Question Answering over Tabular and Textual Data in Finance Thanks: This work is substantially supported by a grant from the Research Grant Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China (Project Code: 14200719) and the Sea-NExT Joint Lab. Wor
arxiv-2210-08817.creator: Yang Deng, Wenqiang Lei, Wenxuan Zhang, Wai Lam, Tat-Seng Chua
arxiv-2210-08817.description: Abstract To facilitate conversational question answering (CQA) over hybrid contexts in finance, we present a new dataset, named PACIFIC. Compared with existing CQA datasets, PACIFIC exhibits three key features: (i) proactivity, (ii) numerical reasoning, and (iii) hybrid context of tables and text.

arxiv-2303-08650.title: Controlled-NOT gate based on the Rydberg states of surface electrons
arxiv-2303-08650.creator: Jun Wang, Wan-Ting He, Cong-Wei Lu, Yang-Yang Wang, Qing Ai, Hai-Bo Wang
arxiv-2303-08650.description: Abstract Due to the long coherence time and efficient manipulation, the surface electron (SE) provides a perfect two-dimensional platform for quantum computation and quantum simulation. In this work, a theoretical scheme to realize the controlled-NOT (CNOT) gate is proposed, where the two-qubit system is encoded on the four-level Rydberg structure of SE.

arxiv-2402-14363.title: Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) for nuclear data evaluation
arxiv-2402-14363.creator: E. Alhassan, D. Rochman, G. Schnabel, A.J. Koning
arxiv-2402-14363.description: Abstract In order to ensure agreement between theoretical model calculations and experimental data, parameters to selected sets of nuclear reaction models coupled together in a nuclear physics code such as TALYS, are usually perturbed and fine-tuned in nuclear data evaluations. This approach assumes that the chosen set of models accurately represents the ‘true’ distribution.

arxiv-2403-02923.title: Galled Tree-Child Networks
arxiv-2403-02923.creator: Yu-Sheng Chang and Michael Fuchs and Guan-Ru Yu
arxiv-2403-02923.description: Abstract We propose the class of galled tree-child networks which is obtained as intersection of the classes of galled networks and tree-child networks. For the latter two classes, (asymptotic) counting results and stochastic results have been proved with very different methods.

arxiv-2410-12614.title: Mixed-precision finite element kernels and assembly: Rounding error analysis and hardware acceleration
arxiv-2410-12614.creator: Matteo Croci, Garth N. Wells
arxiv-2410-12614.description: Abstract In this paper we develop the first fine-grained rounding error analysis of finite element (FE) cell kernels and assembly. The theory includes mixed-precision implementations and accounts for hardware-acceleration via matrix multiplication units, thus providing theoretical guidance for designing reduced- and mixed-precision FE algorithms on CPUs and GPUs.

arxiv-2412-06473.title: Verification of the tenth-Order QED contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the electron from diagrams without fermion loops
arxiv-2412-06473.creator: Tatsumi Aoyama, Masashi Hayakawa, Akira Hirayama, Makiko Nio
arxiv-2412-06473.description: Abstract A discrepancy of approximately 5 σ \sigma exists between the two known results for the tenth-order QED contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the electron, calculated from Feynman vertex diagrams without fermion loops. To investigate this, we decomposed this contribution into 389 parts based on a self-energy diagram representation, enabling a diagram-by-diagram numerical comparison of the two calculations.

arxiv-2508-08336.title: Empirical Bayes for Data integration
arxiv-2508-08336.creator: Paul Rognon-Vael, Pompeu Fabra University and David Rossell, Pompeu Fabra University
arxiv-2508-08336.description: Abstract . We discuss the use of empirical Bayes for data integration, in the sense of transfer learning. Our main interest is in settings where one wishes to learn structure (e.g. feature selection) and one only has access to incomplete data from previous studies, such as summaries, estimates or lists of relevant features.

pmc-10745289.title: Two-Dimensional Transition Metal Boride TMB12 (TM = V, Cr, Mn, and Fe) Monolayers: Robust Antiferromagnetic Semiconductors with Large Magnetic Anisotropy
pmc-10745289.creator: Huiqin Zhang, Nini Guo, Ziyu Wang, Yuqi Xiao, Xiangfei Zhu, Shu Wang, Xiaojing Yao, Yongjun Liu, Xiuyun Zhang, Emmanuel Koudoumas, Reinhard Karl Kremer
pmc-10745289.description: Currently, two-dimensional (2D) materials with intrinsic antiferromagnetism have stimulated research interest due to their insensitivity to external magnetic fields and absence of stray fields. Here, we predict a family of stable transition metal (TM) borides, TMB12 (TM = V, Cr, Mn, Fe) monolayers, by combining TM atoms and B12 icosahedra based on first-principles calculations.

pmc-11556228.title: Feasibility of quick response-based quality improvement projects in an urban primary care setting: A cross-sectional survey
pmc-11556228.creator: Zi-Yi Yeoh, Hooi Chin Beh, Megat Mohamad Amirul Amzar Megat Hashim, Abdul Hadi Haireen, Deik Roy Chuan, Sajaratulnisah Othman
pmc-11556228.description: Introduction:Using quick response (QR) codes to disseminate information has become increasingly popular since the declaration of COVID-19 as a pandemic. We aimed to investigate the feasibility of implementing QR-based quality improvement projects in our clinic to improve patients’ medical knowledge, experience and access to care.

pmc-11579696.title: Systematic deletion of symmetrical CFTR exons reveals new therapeutic targets for exon skipping antisense oligonucleotides
pmc-11579696.creator: Cecilia Pena-Rasgado, Elvia Rodriguez-Manriquez, Miroslav Dundr, Robert J Bridges, Michelle L Hastings, Wren E Michaels
pmc-11579696.description: There is a major need for therapeutics that treat disease caused by premature termination codons (PTCs). Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) can be directed to block splicing and cause exon skipping, a process that can be used to effectively remove PTCs from an mRNA.

pmc-11690234.title: PARTNERS IN DEMENTIA – NORTHWEST: NEW APPROACHES IN MEDICAL STUDENT SERVICE LEARNING
pmc-11690234.creator: Mengru Wang, Michael Rosenbloom, Marigrace Becker, Stephanie Adaniya
pmc-11690234.description: Partners in Dementia – Northwest is the first service-learning program at the University of Washington School of Medicine focused on older adults and persons living with memory loss, established in 2023. First year medical student volunteers, “mentees”, were paired with older adults living with memory loss, “mentors”, recruited from a memory disorders clinic based at the University of Washington.

pmc-11834865.title: High throughput single cell metagenomic sequencing with semi-permeable capsules: unraveling microbial diversity at the single-cell level in sewage and fecal microbiomes
pmc-11834865.creator: Meilee Ling, Judit Szarvas, Vaida Kurmauskaitė, Vaidotas Kiseliovas, Rapolas Žilionis, Baptiste Avot, Patrick Munk, Frank M. Aarestrup
pmc-11834865.description: Single-cell sequencing may serve as a powerful complementary technique to shotgun metagenomics to study microbiomes. This emerging technology allows the separation of complex microbial communities into individual bacterial cells, enabling high-throughput sequencing of genetic material from thousands of singular bacterial cells in parallel.

pmc-12450107.title: Neurosurgery 4.0: A Scoping Review of Current Trends and Challenges in Specialized Smart Hospitals
pmc-12450107.creator: Ehab Shabo, Sevgi Sarikaya-Seiwert, Valeri Borger, Matthias Schneider, Hartmut Vatter, Lutz Hager
pmc-12450107.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The worldwide increase in neurosurgical conditions, due to global population growth and increased life expectancy, challenges healthcare systems, necessitating more precise diagnostics and personalized treatment strategies despite workforce shortages.While rapid technological progress, particularly in the field of artificial intelligence (AI), holds significant promise for enhancing diagnostics, therapeutic strategies, and administrative efficiency in healthcare, there is a marked absence of comprehensive, field-specific analyses addressing these developments within specialized Smart Hospital environments such as neurosurgery centers.

pmc-12663543.title: SKP2 protein as a prognostic biomarker for glioma and promotes tumor progression by regulating the cell cycle
pmc-12663543.creator: Lei Guan, Haima Li, Yezu Liu, Jia Ouyang, Changxiang Yan, Feng Liu
pmc-12663543.description: SKP2 (S-phase kinase-associated protein 2) plays an important role in the regulation of the cell cycle, tumorigenesis, progression, and metastasis. However, its functional role in gliomas is currently unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between SKP2 and the progression of gliomas, and its effects on the glioma cell cycle.

pmc-13674911.creator: Deepsekhar Das, Mandeep Singh Bajaj, Radhika Tandon
pmc-13674911.description: Purpose:To evaluate the feasibility and safety of using the Da Vinci robotic surgical system for simulated eyelid laceration repair in a controlled experimental setting.Methods:A proof-of-concept simulation study was conducted using gloves and sponge. uslaw-usc-t42-s251.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s251.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 6A (Public Health Service); Subchapter II (General Powers And Duties); Part C (Hospitals, Medical Examinations, And Medical Care).
